Subject: Control-plane handback: verification artifacts and acceptable proofs

Hi Olga,

Quick question from our security and procurement reviewers: as part of CloudMed's private VPC onboarding we need clear, auditable proof that when a tenant is decommissioned or we request a handback, Redwood can provide specific artifacts to show customer data was destroyed or handed back to us.

Specifically they're asking for answers to:
- What logs/artifacts do you provide to prove deletion of customer-owned volumes and snapshots?
- If the customer exports a snapshot before deletion, what manifest/verification do you provide so we can validate integrity (hashes, file lists)?
- How do you handle KMS keys for customer-managed keys versus Redwood-managed keys? Can you prove key destruction or rotation?
- Is there a certified attestation you can provide (signed PDF) and what does it include?

We need this at a level that our auditors (external) will accept for HIPAA and SOC2 evidence. Any concise Q&A and an example attestation would help.

Thanks,
Ellen

Hi Ellen,

Thanks for the clear list — great questions. Below is a concise Q&A + an outline of the artifacts we can produce for CloudMed. I also attached a one-page checklist and a draft attestation template (we can customize language for your procurement/legal team).

1) Proofs for deletion of customer-owned volumes/snapshots - We provide an ordered deletion log (timestamped events) showing the deletion calls issued, the resource IDs, and the worker/node identifiers that executed the deletion.
- We can include immutable storage-engine events (object-store tombstone records) and a post-deletion verification pass that scans the namespace to confirm absence.
- Artifact types: deletion-log.csv (signed by our system), object-store tombstone index extract, post-delete verification manifest.

2) Snapshot export verification (customer-led export) - If CloudMed exports a snapshot before deletion, we can: 1) provide a manifest listing exported object keys and sizes, 2) include SHA256 checksums for each exported object, and 3) produce a signed delivery receipt showing the target egress endpoint and timestamp.
- Recommended flow: Customer requests export -> Redwood spawns export job -> export writes to customer-owned S3 (or presigned URL) -> system emits manifest + checksums -> customer verifies locally and confirms.

3) KMS handling (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed keys)
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended for the highest assurance): keys never leave your KMS. Redwood stores only ciphertext; when you request a handback/erase we provide a KMS-side key policy change log and can coordinate key rotation or scheduled key disablement. We can produce KMS audit events showing key disable/destroy requests initiated by the customer.
- Redwood-managed keys: keys are rotated per our operational policy. For destruction proofs, we can provide key lifecycle events and HSM audit logs indicating zeroization requests. Note: some auditors require customer control of keys for strongest proof.

4) Formal attestation and chain-of-custody
- We can produce a Redwood-signed PDF attestation that enumerates the resources deleted and artifacts produced (deletion-log, manifest, checksums, KMS events). The attestation includes a cryptographic hash of the artifacts bundle (SHA256) and a reference to the internal audit record id.
- We can also produce a chain-of-custody CSV showing operator ids (system service accounts), timestamps, and the verification steps executed post-delete.

5) Timeline and retention of evidence
- Immediate artifacts (deletion logs, manifests, KMS events): exported at time of action, retained in your handback package.
- Redwood stores corresponding audit pointers for 90 days by default; we can extend retention of audit pointers/artifacts on request for contractual terms.

6) Auditor-friendly items we recommend including in the handback package
- deletion-log.csv (signed)
- export-manifest.jsonl (with SHA256 per object)
- attestation.pdf (Redwood-signed)
- KMS event export (if customer-managed KMS, KMS-provided key rotation/disable logs)
- manifest hash (single SHA256) and human-readable checklist

Next steps: if this level of proof meets CloudMed's needs, Marissa and Karthik are copied to align on timeline and to provision any additional logs or longer retention. We can also run a short table-top demo of a mock handback to show the artifacts.

If you want, I can also provide redacted examples of the attestation and manifests.

Best,
Olga

Hi Olga — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of clarifying points from our audit team:
- For the deletion-log.csv, can you include a verification signature or HMAC we can validate against a public key? They prefer a signature over a simple CSV.
- For KMS customer-managed flows, our ops team will need a documented handshake: which API calls do we call to request key-disable and what artifact will KMS return that you will include in the attestation?

Also, procurement wants to know if Redwood would add a one-off 180-day retention for the evidence artifacts (attestation + logs) tied to our contract for the onboarding wave. Is that feasible, and what would be the expected lead time?

If you can provide short answers to the two points and confirm the 180-day retention option, Procurement can move forward this week.

Thanks — Ellen

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Ellen — quick answers inline and next steps.

- Signed deletion-log: we can produce a deletion-log.csv and sign it with a Redwood-service PGP key or issue an HMAC computed with a per-contract verification key. If you prefer signature verification, we'll include our public key and a signature block (PGP ASCII-armored) in the handback package.

- KMS handshake (customer-managed): typical flow we recommend:
  1) Customer initiates key-disable via their KMS console/API and notifies Redwood via the handback ticket.
  2) Redwood polls the KMS audit API (or you provide KMS event export) to capture the key-disable/key-schedule event.
  3) Redwood bundles the KMS audit snippet (signed by KMS) into the attestation and references the KMS event id.

  Artifacts returned by KMS: key-rotation/disable event id, timestamp, and KMS-signed audit record (many KMSes provide a JSON audit event signed by the provider). We will include that JSON as-is in the attestation bundle.

- 180-day retention option: yes, we can contractually extend evidence artifact retention to 180 days. Lead time: typically 5 business days after contract amendment to enable extended retention in our evidence-store and to add the retention flag to your tenant. We'll provide a change-order and an estimated cost (small per-MB archival fee) for procurement.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa will draft a short Service Addendum language for the 180-day evidence retention and a sample attestation clause.
2) Karthik will schedule a 30-min table-top demo where we perform a mock handback and show the actual artifacts.
3) If acceptable, we'll deliver a redacted attestation + sample deletion-log for your audit team to validate.

I'm copying Marissa and Karthik to pick up the two action items.
